steps.text: In my memories, I see a vast field of snow.
I remember when I was little, I sat on a wooden bed. The fireplace crackled, while a snowstorm blew outside.
The sound of the wind whispered into my ears. There was a large hand stroking my head, and there was someone putting me to bed.
And I drifted off to sleep in that warm, calming sensation.
I used to think that was Ursus.
But Mamochka told me: Nyet, Rosalind, that wasn't Ursus.
That was Kjerag wind.
That was Kjerag snow.
That... was where I was born.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: So... It wasn't until you entered secondary school that you learned you were born in Kjerag?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: That's right. Mamochka never told me before. I thought she was kidding at first!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I don't remember much of my childhood. All I can picture is snow everywhere... And there's snow everywhere in Ursus, too!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: How was I supposed to know?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hm, now that you mention it, they are alike in that way.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: However, from what I remember, Ursus is colder than Kjerag.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hm... That is true. Ursus's colder.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Have you been?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hah, many years ago.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I didn't have much chance to sightsee, though. What a shame!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Then I'll be your guide the next time you visit.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Forget the rest of Ursus, Deity Grypherburg is a sight in itself.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Very well, then. Seems I may have to get myself a couple of coats to keep me warm.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But until I have the opportunity to visit Ursus and take you up on the offer, let me be your guide instead.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'll start by telling you about this train's destination—the newly built statue of Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It is built atop the island in the middle of Lake Silberneherze. Very conspicuous. You'll see it as soon as you step outside the station.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Of course, for you, the statue is not the point of your trip...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You came to Kjerag for something more important than sightseeing.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Yeah, sure did.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I need to take a good look at the Kjeragandr statue for my mamochka, though. It's... It's something she stressed before she left us.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Then, I'll head up the mountain next to Lake Silberneherze.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I need to take the box to the peak.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: What's inside?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: No idea. She never told me.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: She just said I had to dump what's inside on the mountain, and that she'd be satisfied if I did.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Coming to your foreign homeland all by yourself only to fulfill your mother's wishes...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: What a kind, faithful daughter! It moves my very soul!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Eh, that's really too much.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: What are your plans after that?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: After I take this up the mountain? I'm not too sure. I might travel around.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I might... look for my papa.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Is your father still in Kjerag?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Perhaps I could offer my assistance in searching for him?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: For real? But I don't even know his name, and I don't remember what he looks like.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: But Mamochka told me he was very handsome.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Aha, a handsome fellow.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Yeah! I guess he used to be a famous, handsome guy. Like, pretty popular, too.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Oh, right, and she told me my eyes look just like his.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: A famous, handsome man from Kjerag? Hm...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Do you know anybody like that?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: To have a daughter your age, he could only have done the deed while studying in Victoria... Hm...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: No. No, no, no. That would be far too outrageous...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ursus in those days... Could it be...?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Could it be what?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Uh, hah, I must give this some more thought.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I really hope we'll be able to find him.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You're hoping for a touching father-daughter reunion?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Ugh.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Not exactly.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: All I want is to see what this bastard who's been gone for over a decade even looks like.

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Welcome aboard the new Saintess Express. Our train has reached cruising speed. You may appreciate the finest natural sights that Kjerag has to offer through the windows on both sides of the train.

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: During our journey, we have a variety of local Kjerag delicacies available for purchase!

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: From all our favorite treats like yogurt snacks to the ever popular burdenbeast blind boxes, and even Karlan Trade's limited edition mountain ice waters, everything we have on offer is produced locally, handpicked by the Saintess herself, and guaranteed to be of the finest quality!

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Please feel free to browse our selections...

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: Excuse me. I have a question.

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Ah, what can I get you today, good sir?

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: I'm not buying anything.

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: These delicacies are not to your fancy? How about this limited edition mountain ice water?

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: This is the Tri-Clan's official drinking water, and it's the Saintess's personal favorite. We don't have many in stock today. A rare opportunity. It can be yours right now for just four francs!

steps.name: Spectating Passenger
steps.text: Holy Saintess... four francs? I could buy out a restaurant for that price!

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: It's a little pricey, but just look at the packaging. This clean, pure sensation. It's a perfect fit for your splendid appearance!

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: ...I'll pass.

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: I'll... take a blind box. Thank you.

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Thank you very much!

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: How long until the next station?

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: This train is a nonstop limited express. The next stop will be the terminus, Lake Silberneherze.

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: We are about two hours from our destination!

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: If you would like to stop somewhere during our journey to better take in the sights along the way, we also offer regular trains that stop at every station on the route!

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: Okay, thank you.

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: You are very welcome.

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Blind box? Are these trinkets really so popular?)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (It's just a meaningless ornament, no matter how I look at it.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Still two hours to go. That's more than enough time.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Next... Hm?)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: A fowlbeast?

steps.name: Runaway Fowlbeast
steps.text: (Pecks fiercely)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: What...?!

steps.name: Runaway Fowlbeasts
steps.text: (Fly everywhere)

steps.name: Runaway Fowlbeasts
steps.text: (Attack all over)

steps.name: Runaway Fowlbeasts
steps.text: Gkh—Gkhhh!

steps.name: Shocked Villager
steps.text: Eh, my fowlbeasts! How did they get out?

steps.name: Passionate Villager
steps.text: Where? I'll help you catch them!

steps.name: Meddlesome Villager
steps.text: I'll help, too!

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Mom, I want to catch fowlbeasts!

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (...Not good.)

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Hey, mister! Where are you going?

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Why don't you help?

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Catching fowlbeasts is so much fun!

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Phew.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (To think mere fowlbeasts and a toddler could be so fierce together.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Seems Kjerag isn't to be underestimated.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (But this does give me a legitimate excuse to check the train cars.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: Good afternoon, sirs, have any of you seen any runaway fowlbeasts?

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: No? Thank you. Sorry for disturbing you.

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Nothing out of the ordinary here.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Nothing strange in the car up ahead, either. Only the last few cabins left.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Looks like this will be another futile journey.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: Excuse me, have you...?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: ...If I find him, I'll make him pay for that decade!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Look at this. Before I came here, I had Natalya and Anna—they're my friends, you see. I asked them to help me math all this out.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Living expenses, education, medical—oh, and this 'emotional absenteeism' fee that Natalya came up with. It's all here.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Doesn't matter how good-looking he is! It's not like that ever fed me!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hahahahaha, emotional absenteeism. Not bad. Very good. I approve!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hm? A guest? Please...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: ...come in...

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: ...Have you seen any escaped fowlbeasts?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Fowlbeasts? Oh, I saw one earlier...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ah, right, of course! We did see one!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Come, come, come, good sir. Let us head outside and discuss that fowlbeast in the greatest detail!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Huh? What detail is there to a—

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: What the heck? Why are they acting so funny?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hm... Victorians. I hope everything's okay...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Alright, kind sir, shall we discuss the fowlbeast?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm very curious what kind of fowlbeast would require a Trilby Asher coming to me in person.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I did not expect to find you on this train, Lord Viscount.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh, please. I could say the very same. Minus the viscount bit.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Why is it that I've never noticed that the Trilby Ashers had such an interest in sightseeing? Or is it that your early retirement has finally been approved?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Seems not.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: No need for the interrogation, My Lord.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I'm merely doing a routine investigation on certain rumors that I've heard.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Now, I can't say I buy that.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You and I both help lift the weight off Her Grace. We should have more trust in one another.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: What about you, My Lord? What is your purpose here? And the young lady with you... Is she Ursine?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: She looks a little familiar.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Trilby Asher...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I must say. If that was an attempt to make a move on the lady, it was rather behind the times.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: That is not my intention at all, but thank you for the reminder.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: As for me. I am, of course, sightseeing.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Are you?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Mind your words now. We should have more trust in one another!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: The Kjeragandr statue ceremony is in two days. I received an invitation, and I thought I ought to do a little sightseeing before the unveiling.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I bought two small Saintess sculptures that I am bringing with me on the day. Pretty well-made, if you ask me.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Anyway, enough chit-chat. I see no... 'fowlbeasts' here.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You should get back to work, Trilby Asher.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You too, My Lord.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I hope you haven't forgotten why we're here.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (This is the last one. Nothing out of the ordinary.)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (Except Viscount Craigavon and the girl with him...)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (That one traveling with the Viscount... Who exactly is she? It seems I must look into this once I get back.)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (But first, I should finish checking this last cabin—)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Pardon—

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Please excuse me.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: No, that's impossible.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: The intel says she is training new recruits in the mountains. She can't be here.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: She shouldn't be...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Need something?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If you need something, out with it. Or is it so much fun to open random doors?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (It really is her...?! The Black Knight who works for the Silverashes...?)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (There are bloodstains on her hands. Who forced her hand?)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (...This is bad.)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: (But this also means the intel's not wrong. There's trouble on this route.)

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: No, before I consider that...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Who are the intelligence officers in charge of watching Degenbrecher...?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Ah, there we are.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: For them to miss such an important piece of information... They can expect to see a court-martial.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Intelligence officers, you say?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Don't blame them. There aren't many who can keep up with me.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Thank you for speaking up for them.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's the truth.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Now, tell me what you're doing here.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Surely you must have already come up with an excuse or two?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Trilby Asher?
